reference.title: Cable Alternate Triceps Extension
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching: alternating one-arm pushdowns with a D-handle in each hand)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as each handle goes down, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s down, short pause, about 1.8 s up, each arm in turn

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can push down with the working elbow still at your side for every rep.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower return.

cues.text: Face the high pulley, feet hip width, slight forward lean; a D-handle in each hand, palms down, elbows at your sides and bent about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and push the right handle down until the arm is straight; the left arm holds at 90 degrees.
Squeeze the back of the right arm, hand beside the thigh, wrist straight.
Breathe in and let the right handle rise slowly back to 90 degrees; the elbow stays pinned.
Now push the left handle down while the right arm holds at 90 degrees.
Squeeze the back of the left arm, shoulders level, trunk square.
Let the left handle rise slowly back to 90 degrees.
Brief pause with both elbows at 90 degrees, then start again with the right arm.

mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow against your side; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting or tilting the trunk toward the working arm
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips and shoulders square to the tower; the resting arm holds still at 90 degrees.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the handle fly up past 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Control the return and stop when the forearm is about level.
Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees to straight (clinical opinion)
Upper arm along the trunk and still; with the arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018)
Palm down on a D-handle in each hand (clinical opinion)
Upright or slightly forward, square to the tower and still while the arms alternate (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Alternate Triceps Extension, video (movement reference)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position (Eur J Sport Sci 2022, DOI 10.1080/17461391.2022.2100279; PubMed 35819335; 21 adults, 12 weeks, cable)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with the elbows still.
Stand close enough that the cable runs in front of the shoulder and face, not into them.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow pain: use a lighter load and a shorter range (clinical opinion).
Wrist discomfort: turn the palm in (neutral grip) or use a rope end.
regressions: One-arm pushdown with the free hand on the hip.
progressions: Overhead cable triceps extension (more triceps growth than the arm-at-the-side position in a 12-week study, PubMed 35819335).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the cable, each arm in turn while the other holds at 90 degrees. With the upper arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018); training in this position gave less triceps growth than overhead extensions in a 12-week study (PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the cable, each arm in turn while the other holds at 90 degrees. With the upper arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018); training in this position gave less triceps growth than overhead extensions in a 12-week study (PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Holds the upper arm against the side so the elbow stays pinned.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Holds the upper arm against the side so the elbow stays pinned.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Keeps the upper arm from drifting forward.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Keeps the upper arm from drifting forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still and square so body weight does not push the handle.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keep the trunk from twisting toward the working arm.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keep the trunk from twisting toward the working arm.

guides.label: Right forearm swings down, elbow still
